title: Why most people will never truly own Bitcoin
tweets:
Bitcoin ownership isn't binary.

There's a spectrum — and most people who think they "own Bitcoin" are somewhere in the middle of it, mistaking exposure for possession.

Here's what the spectrum actually looks like. 🧵

At one end: a Bitcoin ETF.

You own shares in a fund that claims to hold Bitcoin. BlackRock holds the keys. You hold a financial instrument regulated by the SEC, redeemable on their terms.

This is the furthest possible distance from Bitcoin ownership.

In the middle: exchange accounts, custodial apps, institutional wallets.

A company holds your keys. You have a balance, a login, and a withdrawal button that works — until it doesn't.

Most people stop here and call it done.

At the other end: you hold the keys.

A hardware wallet in your possession. A seed phrase only you have ever seen. No company between you and your Bitcoin.

No approval process. No withdrawal limits. No terms of service.

The psychological barrier is real.

Self-custody requires accepting full responsibility. No customer support if you lose the seed phrase. No chargebacks. No one to call.

Most people want the upside of Bitcoin without the weight of owning it. So they delegate — and lose what makes it worth owning.

The question isn't whether you have Bitcoin exposure.

It's: if every exchange, ETF, and custodian shut down tomorrow — would you still have Bitcoin?

That answer tells you where you actually are on the spectrum.
